jitasm_2018-11-24_mingw13_x64_jitasm.dll.license: New BSD (three-clause), Copyright (c) 2009-2011 Hikaru Inoue, Akihiro Yamasaki
jitasm_2018-11-24_mingw13_x64_jitasm.dll.notes: Built from an exerciser translation unit, since the library is one header: upstream's test/test_backend.cpp, included unmodified, supplies sixty instruction-family structs that the exerciser assembles, and seven functions of its own reach the register allocator, control flow and calling conventions. Measured at -O2 on this compiler: 1563 functions kept of 1617 on x86 (54 MinGW runtime removed), 1867 of 1922 on x64 (55), 1308 and 1627 of them ten instructions or more. -O0 gives 12489 text symbols against 3925 at -O2 on x64 (11634 against 3235 on x86), so the library survives optimisation and the artefact does not describe an unoptimised consumer. About one function in eight is not jitasm's: the sixty test_*::naked_main bodies are upstream's test cases and, with the exerciser's ex_* and assemble_one functions and the <iostream> static initialiser, 197 functions on x86 and 252 on x64 are consumer code recognisable by name. The MSVC and ELF counterparts are built from the same exerciser and share no PicHash with this one at the ten-instruction floor (4 of 863 on x86 against the ELF build). Evidence behind the family is structural only: Kaspersky describes jitasm building NtOpenProcessToken and NtAdjustPrivilegesToken syscall stubs and publishes no function, constant or table.

jitasm_2018-11-24_msvc143_x64_jitasm.dll.notes: The same exerciser translation unit as the MinGW build, so the two differ in the compiler. Measured at /O2: 5519 functions kept of 7148 on x86 (1629 MSVC runtime removed), 6098 of 7795 on x64 (1697), 4230 and 4415 of them ten instructions or more, all named; 4877 and 5311 carry jitasm in their name. Roughly one in fourteen is not jitasm's: the sixty test_*::naked_main bodies from upstream's test/test_backend.cpp and the exerciser's own ex_*, assemble_one and test_backend functions, 336 on x86 and 483 on x64, recognisable by name. No /Od build: /O2 keeps the whole library, so there is no unoptimised consumer to describe. PicHash overlap with the MinGW and ELF builds is zero at the ten-instruction floor on both architectures. The MSVC STL's __std_remove_4 and __std_remove_8 survive the glue filter on x64.
